title: hla-wgs: HLA typing from whole-genome sequencing with a per-allele statement of what is certain
description:
Single Rust program that types 18 HLA genes (A, B, C, DRB1, DRB3, DRB4, DRB5, DQA1, DQB1, DPA1, DPB1, DRA, E, F, G, H, K, V) from short-read whole-genome sequencing (FASTQ, BAM or CRAM), with its own aligner and no external tool or interpreter at run time. For every allele it reports the best four-field name, the resolution up to which the call is certain, copy number for DRB3/4/5, H and K, and the positions at which the reads differ from the named allele (candidate new alleles). The reference database is built locally from the IPD-IMGT/HLA release with hla-wgs build-db; no IPD-IMGT/HLA sequences are distributed.

Validation: on 80 haplotype-resolved HPRC genomes 2486 of 2489 alleles are right at two fields and 1780 of 1799 certain four-field calls are exact; on 59 unseen HGSVC3 genomes 1334 of 1350 certain four-field calls are exact; against the laboratory typing of 967 1000 Genomes samples (Abi-Rached et al. 2018) 9051 of 9090 two-field alleles agree. Lower depth (10x, 15x) and PacBio HiFi long reads (experimental hla-wgs long) are evaluated as well.

New in 1.2.0: more precise DRB1, more certain calls at low depth, a run log with stable error codes, a report part in the Genome format genome.report.v1 (German and English), an MCP server for agents, a complete manual, validation and report built entirely in Rust, and faster typing with unchanged results. Research use only.
